stories.Headline: Tampa Bay professors split on whether AI harms the arts as some teach AI tools
stories.Summary:
The Tampa Bay Times reported on November 25, 2026, that Tampa Bay professors are mixed on whether AI is destroying the arts. The article was written by reporter Lucy Marques. It was published in the Times’ Education Gradebook section. Govtech.com republished the story on November 24, 2026, credited to Lucy Marques of the Tampa Bay Times. The articles talked with five Tampa Bay professors who teach English, music, film and art history.

The articles name five professors. Santiago Echeverry, 56, teaches film at the University of Tampa. Tom Hallock has worked three decades at the University of South Florida. Steven Lewis, 37, is a USF music professor. Sheila Levi-Aland, 46, is a professor at St. Petersburg College.

Anuj Gupta, 34, is a USF English professor. Echeverry pitched a class called AI: Imaging the Future to the university’s trustees last year. Lewis teaches Artificial Intelligence in Music. Gupta teaches Writing with AI. Echeverry requires students to turn in chat logs that can stretch to over 100 pages.

Levi-Aland noticed in 2022 that one of her students had used generative AI to complete a project. Hallock offers extra credit if students draft with typewriters. Echeverry said filmmakers should use whatever tools they have to keep up. He said he cried when he first saw a student’s AI-made song and video about a college graduate. He said he wonders if more artists will find their purpose dancing, making sculptures and painting.

Hallock said it feels like a broken trust to have to read auto-generated writing. He said he feels more like a cop than a teacher when grading papers. Hallock said AI is really only a tool and cited Henry David Thoreau. Lewis said what one person finds value in is going to be completely dismissed by someone else. Lewis said a class on AI in music introduces a completely different way of thinking about music.

Levi-Aland said the biggest reason she keeps doing this is because you need to learn to experiment and enjoy. She said getting your hands dirty is really the way. Gupta said students are overwhelmed with AI tools and hear conflicting narratives. Gupta said he predicts more people will be able to access writing and learn to write because of AI. The articles said many artists and writers were quick to call generated content “slop” that at best lacks creativity and humanity.

The articles said some humanities professors say their students are vehemently against using AI. The articles said most of the five professors have mixed feelings about AI. The articles said some are diving in by teaching classes on how AI tools can support artists and writers. The articles said others are staying away from it and returning to traditional assignments like annotating physical books. The articles said Florida colleges are preparing students for an AI-era workforce.

The articles said many professors believe artificial intelligence can benefit industries like healthcare, technology and manufacturing. The articles said there is more skepticism in the arts and humanities. The articles said AI chatbots came on the scene four years ago. Levi-Aland said she was livid that a student literally put a project in AI and didn’t do a single thing. She said a student once challenged her on the date of a historical event, and a chatbot gave the student’s answer, pulling from an old and outdated website.

She said it is worrying that students rely on AI for the truth. She said AI can be a helpful tool for artists to market their work. Gupta said he teaches the differences between cognitive offloading and uploading. He said cognitive offloading is when technology handles mental labor, like having our phone store numbers or using Google Maps. He said cognitive uploading is when technology builds on our opportunities to think.

He said if we offload for a lot of meaningful tasks like writing, we lose out on opportunities to build our critical thinking. He said he is guessing that in the next few years we will reach some sort of equilibrium as these tools become a regular part of our lives. Echeverry said that in the next few years filmmakers will reckon with AI tools that can create more efficiently than they can. He said the discussion comes up often in class because everyone’s future jobs are at stake. He said anything that is going to be electronically based is going to be controlled by AI.

Lewis said he understands why some students are apprehensive to discuss or use AI tools, especially because there is now software that uncannily reproduces their work. He said if we are worried about AI-generated music being able to reproduce what we can already do, perhaps this is a catalyst to recognize or create completely new ways of musicking. Hallock said he does not want to be paranoid about the change AI brings. Gupta said he thinks we are currently in a phase where there is a lot of criticism and a lot of issues coming up.

stories.Headline: Congress introduces four bills to block Chinese access to US computing power
stories.Summary:
Congress introduced four bills to stop Chinese access to American computing power. These legislative efforts occurred in late 2026 during a shift in political power. The bills target chip licensing, diversion after sale, chipmaking equipment, and remote rentals. Three of these measures are part of a Senate defense authorization package. Congress expects to take up this package in December.

The AI OVERWATCH Act would codify bans on advanced chip sales to countries of concern. It gives Congress 30 days to block transactions, which the president could then veto. The Chip Security Act requires location verification for covered chips within 180 days. The MATCH Act targets chipmaking equipment and sets a 150 day deadline for allies. RASA would allow the Department of Commerce to license remote access to controlled items.

The bills represent a rebuke of President Donald Trump's approach to the AI race. Trump claimed the government has no reason to believe Jensen Huang poses a security risk. The Department of Commerce issued a rule regarding Chinese firms renting capacity from third countries. Some critics object to the strict deadlines imposed on the Netherlands and Japan. The House passed RASA 369 to 22 in January.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was reinstated on Monday after resigning on November 12. He resigned over reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, a former Singapore executive. US officials suspect Alice Huang of diverting chips to China and working for Chinese intelligence. The Nvidia board acted after receiving input from senior US officials. These events provide the backdrop for the current legislative efforts in Congress.

The bills assume that access to computing power decides the outcome of the AI race. This premise is one that the Trump administration has rejected in recent years. The administration prioritizes securing global market share over limiting adversarial access to advanced chips. Some technology leaders believe the race depends on who builds the best applications. Chinese efforts to smuggle chips suggest they believe computing power is the deciding factor.

Congress will decide if RASA is included in the National Defense Authorization Act. The effectiveness of the Commerce rule depends on future enforcement and administration willingness. It remains uncertain if the AI frontier is decided by computing power or applications. The bills may undermine efforts to seize global market share by limiting sales. The articles leave open whether the president will veto congressional resolutions to block sales.

stories.Headline: Woman says AI-driven system led to her eviction over unpaid rent
stories.Summary:
A woman says an AI-driven nightmare led to her eviction from her apartment when she thought she had until the end of the month to pay her overdue rent, according to reports published on Nov. 24, 2026 at 3:40 AM EST. The articles do not name the woman, the apartment, the city or the company behind the AI system, and they give no further details about what the system did or when the eviction took place. The only account the articles give is her statement that she believed she had until the end of the month to pay the overdue rent. The story was carried by several local news sites, each running the same short account with the same publication time. The articles do not say what the eviction requires of her, what it changes, or which law or process applies, and they give no numbers, dates or names beyond the Nov. 24, 2026 publication time.

No figure for the overdue rent, no deadline and no court date appears in any of the four versions. The articles also do not say whether the AI system set the deadline, sent a notice or took some other step. Because the reports stop at her statement, there is nothing further to describe about what the eviction involves. The articles do not identify who is responsible for the eviction or for the AI system, and they include no statement from a landlord, a property manager, a court or a technology company. The woman is the only person the articles attribute any statement to, and the only words they give her are that she thought she had until the end of the month to pay.

No official commented on the case in the articles, and no one else was named in connection with it. The articles give no context about how the AI system was used in the rental or eviction process, and they do not say what happens next for the woman or for anyone else involved. They do not report whether she is challenging the eviction, whether she has found other housing or whether any agency is looking into the matter. The surrounding items on each site cover unrelated local news, such as weather, school funding and community events, and none of them adds to this story. The reports end with her account and give no follow-up.

stories.Headline: YYForce deploys a trained humanoid concierge robot at Novotel Singapore on Stevens
stories.Summary:
YYForce Inc., which trades on the NASDAQ as YFOR, announced the launch of a proprietary trained humanoid robot on November 24, 2026. This company provides facility solutions, robotics, and an AI enabled frontline workforce to various industries across Asia and other global regions. The new robot was specifically built to handle live hospitality concierge operations within a real world, guest facing hotel service environment. This launch represents a milestone in moving commercial embodied AI from training environments into the active service of hotel guests. The company developed this technology to transform frontline work through the use of intelligent software and commercial robotics.

The first humanoid concierge, named Six Seven or 67, will be deployed at the Novotel Singapore on Stevens hotel. This robot utilizes NVIDIA Jetson edge AI computing and NVIDIA Isaac Sim simulation workflows to achieve reliable performance in public spaces. It is integrated into the Workforce OS architecture to combine natural conversational intelligence with real time property and local knowledge. The system uses NVIDIA Isaac Sim for synthetic training and physical AI simulation to ensure the robot functions in dynamic spaces. NVIDIA Jetson provides the onboard edge AI inference and real time voice interaction required for low latency guest engagement.

Mike Fu serves as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of YYForce and spoke about the new robot deployment. He stated that the deployment at Novotel Singapore on Stevens will demonstrate that humanoid robotics can deliver accuracy and operational value. Fu claimed that the robot can provide genuine warmth on the hotel front line while addressing persistent frontline staffing challenges. He noted that using NVIDIA Jetson and Isaac Sim within the Workforce OS platform accelerates the commercial rollout of embodied AI. This technology is intended to empower hospitality partners to elevate the experiences of their guests through advanced robotic service.

The robot is designed to assist hotel guests by providing immediate answers regarding on site restaurants, venue locations, and dining menus. It can inform visitors about operating hours, daily hotel events, and various activities available at the property for the guests. The robot also provides Singapore wide travel guidance, including neighborhood navigation, transportation options, and curated tourism recommendations for the visitors. Families and guests are affected by the robot's ability to respond to open ended inquiries and provide interactive storytelling experiences. These features are intended to create a memorable arrival experience for every person who enters the hotel lobby area.

YYForce has conducted dedicated robotics training and data collection initiatives in Singapore and Malaysia to support this specific humanoid robot project. The company operates a portfolio that includes digital estate management through 24iFM and intelligent workforce matching via YY Circle and Yolara AI. Their broader business strategy involves the deployment, leasing, and maintenance of service robots for retail, logistics, and integrated facility management. The company aims to build a future where people and intelligent technology thrive together to improve overall business productivity. This mission drives their effort to create a smarter and more sustainable workforce through the use of connected ecosystems.

YYForce plans to scale its commercial service robots across the hospitality, retail, and integrated facility management environments in the coming future. The company will continue to use third party AI computing and simulation technologies to advance its broader commercial robotics strategy. However, the articles leave open whether the robot will maintain safety and reliability when operating in unpredictable public environments. There are also unanswered questions regarding the accuracy of AI generated responses and the requirements for personal data protection and privacy. Finally, the timing of future deployments and the level of customer acceptance remain uncertain factors for the company's growth.

stories.Headline: Trump and Vance reinstate Jensen Huang to protect American open weight AI models
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over a recent weekend. People familiar with the matter said the leaders acted because they believed Huang alone protected American open-weight AI models. This intervention occurred after Huang had resigned as CEO earlier in November 2026 following reports of several extramarital affairs. One of these alleged affairs was reportedly with a Chinese spy, which led to his initial departure from the company. The reinstatement was announced on Monday, November 23, 2026, after the Nvidia board voted unanimously to bring him back.

The board reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and board director after they found that he posed no national security risk. This move helped add one trillion dollars to the stock value of Nvidia, with shares jumping over thirty percent. On October 8, 2026, Trump presented Huang with the National Medal of Science at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace. This event took place in Washington, DC, during a summit titled A New Golden Age at the renamed institute. Huang had previously gestured during the NVIDIA GTC global AI conference in San Jose, California, on March 17, 2026.

President Trump claimed that he made the deal to ensure that Jensen Huang returned to his leadership role at Nvidia. Vice President JD Vance also helped push the company board to bring back the chief executive to protect American interests. Huang had previously written a letter to US lawmakers urging them to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight AI technology. The administration believes that these open-weight models are critical for the United States to better counter the influence of China. These leaders view the availability of such models as a necessary component for maintaining a competitive edge in AI.

Two leading House Republican lawmakers called on the administration to help American companies that are developing these open-weight AI models. These lawmakers argued that supporting such technology would position the United States to better compete against the advancements made by China. The growth of open-weight systems creates a major business opportunity for Nvidia by broadening the demand for its computing infrastructure. Users can download, modify, and adapt these systems, making them cheaper than proprietary tools from labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. This shift affects large AI developers and the broader ecosystem of developers who use platforms like Hugging Face.

Nvidia has been a prominent backer of the US open-weight ecosystem and agreed to buy the platform Hugging Face in August. The company is also an investor in Reflection AI, an American firm that launched its first open-weight model in October. China currently leads in the development of open-weight AI systems, which perform nearly as well as top US proprietary tools. On November 18, reports indicated the Trump administration considered requiring companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This effort aims to reduce the reliance of American technology companies on software and models developed within China.

The US government will now blacklist the Asian AI firm Megaspeed after it was accused of funneling chips to China. This action follows the public disclosure of a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang, which created a significant corporate scandal. The articles leave open how the US will specifically enforce the disclosure of Chinese AI models among various American companies. It remains unclear if further investigations into national security risks will be conducted regarding other executives in the AI sector. The long term impact of the board's unanimous decision on Nvidia's corporate governance and stability is not detailed.

stories.Headline: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang cites Anthropic proof of Riemann Hypothesis to argue superintelligence is near
stories.Summary:
Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, warned on Sunday that superintelligence is arriving, and he built his case on a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number problem. The proof was produced at rival Anthropic, and Wang's essay asks the AI industry to change course. Wang runs Meta's own superintelligence lab, and Meta shareholders are funding that push with up to $145 billion in capital spending this year. The essay never names the proof or its author. The claim arrived one day after Anthropic's $1.5 trillion debut on Nasdaq.

On November 20, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he found the proof while working with Claude, the company's AI model. The Lean and Mathlib communities, which maintain software that machine-checks proofs, certified the result on November 21. Wang says the proof came with help from an "alien mind" humans do not understand. Wang also calls the problem perhaps the hardest humanity has devised. The essay does not spell out what Meta would do differently from the "default path" it criticizes.

Wang argues the scientific problems behind AI capability gains are now likely solved, and he expects models to automate AI research itself. Even so, he rejects the view that artificial superintelligence is simply inevitable, writing that society should resist ceding control. Wang said he notices "a particular form of lazy thinking within the AI industry," which holds that ASI is inevitable and the only problem is how to do it safely. He said there is much more at stake and that we should not be okay with a "handover" of society to AI. His employer, however, is spending at full speed on that same race.

Abhishek Saha, a mathematics professor at Queen Mary University of London, credited Alpöge instead of an alien mind. Saha said others with similar access to frontier AI models and computing resources were not able to come up with a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Meta's third-quarter report showed $34.91 billion in capital expenditures over three months, pushing free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion. That money is building the data center capacity Meta uses to train AI models and run its core business. The company expects full-year 2026 capital spending of $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta also plans to cut Reality Labs losses next year by shifting investment toward AI. It is creating a new class of stock, partly to raise capital for that buildout. Mark Zuckerberg framed those results as progress toward personal superintelligence for everyone. The question of what Meta would do differently now sits with Meta shareholders funding the same race their AI chief wants rerouted. Wang's essay asks the AI industry to change course while he runs Meta's own superintelligence lab.

stories.Headline: US Department of Commerce plans to blacklist Singaporean AI firm Megaspeed over chip export violations
stories.Summary:
The United States government intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence company from doing business in America following a recent Nvidia scandal. The US Department of Commerce announced this plan on Monday to blacklist the firm known as Megaspeed Ltd from American trade. This action follows accusations that a former executive of the company worked as a spy for China during a romantic relationship. The relationship was with Jensen Huang, who is the head of Nvidia, and it led to increased scrutiny by US officials. This situation created heightened concerns that the company was funneling advanced AI computer chips from Nvidia into the country of China.

The Commerce Department plans to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are banned from buying or selling US goods. This Singaporean company is mainly a developer of data centres and has significant business dealings in China with the retailer Alibaba. The US intelligence apparatus believes that Alice Huang, a former executive, was working as an asset for the government in Beijing. This specific relationship between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang became public through media reports that emerged during the previous month. The US has blocked China from buying this specific type of advanced AI technology since the year 2022.

The US Department of Commerce stated that it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years before the affair incident occurred. Officials said they suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping Chinese companies obtain advanced chips from Nvidia. President Donald Trump said he convinced the company and made a deal to reinstate Jensen Huang on Monday after his resignation. The board of Nvidia then reinstated the CEO after the intervention by the president of the United States regarding the matter. The White House, the Commerce Department, and Megaspeed were all asked for comment by the BBC regarding the planned ban.

China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy and warned the US not to use this scandal as a pretext. The Chinese government stated that the US should not use the situation to impose a technological blockade on AI technology. The US intelligence apparatus claims that the activities of Alice Huang created national security concerns within the United States of America. The company Megaspeed was not well known within the US until the media reports about the affair surfaced last month. Another alleged affair involving Jensen Huang also surfaced days after the first one, which led to the CEO's initial resignation.

The US government suspects that Megaspeed was helping to get Nvidia chips into the hands of various companies located within China. This activity would violate US export controls that have been in place to restrict Chinese access to AI technology since 2022. Megaspeed is based in Singapore, but its largest customer is the major Chinese online retailer known as Alibaba. The company primarily focuses on the development of data centres as its main business activity before the recent blacklist announcement. The US intelligence community viewed the romantic link between the two individuals as a risk to national security interests.

The US government has not yet specified when the ban against Megaspeed Ltd will officially go into effect for the company. The Commerce Department continues to monitor the situation after its two year investigation into the suspected violation of export controls. The articles leave open whether the US will impose further restrictions on other companies tied to the recent Nvidia scandal. It remains unclear if the Chinese government will take further diplomatic actions in response to the planned American technological blockade. The BBC is waiting for responses from the White House and Megaspeed regarding the announcement made on Monday.

stories.Headline: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo to block Linux exploits before patches arrive
stories.Summary:
OpenAI and Cisco released an open-source approach called Shirudo on November 24, 2026, to block exploits before patches are ready. This new tool creates shields to protect vulnerable systems while security teams work on developing and rolling out longer-term fixes. The project aims to widen the timeframe for patching by blocking malicious behavior that exposes a vulnerability in the system. It allows legitimate requests to pass through while stopping the specific malicious input that an exploit depends on for success. These AI-powered shields are designed to keep critical systems running without requiring a full shutdown during the deployment process.

Shirudo runs on Linux systems and is an open-source platform licensed under the BSD 2-Clause to encourage wide community use. Many of these shields operate inside the operating system core using a technology known as extended Berkeley Packet Filter, or eBPF. The system was tested on the Java4Shell vulnerability using Codex agents on the Java language based Elasticsearch data search platform. This specific test showed the shield rejected malicious input and blocked the attack while the Elasticsearch platform continued running normally. The tool is designed to work with cyber-capable AI models like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra or Anthropic's Mythos 5.

Greg Brockman, the president and co-founder of OpenAI, stated in a blog post that finding a bug does not mean patching. He explained that OpenAI is partnering with Cisco to help teams protect necessary systems while they build and roll out fixes. Brockman noted that many teams rely on the same software, which makes it logical to build these security tools in the open. The companies invited infrastructure operators, security researchers, and other developers to contribute to and iterate on the work for Shirudo. They stated that the goal is to make tested shields available alongside the disclosure of new vulnerabilities to the public.

Security teams are the primary group affected because they are already overwhelmed by the growing number of vulnerabilities found by AI. These teams are being encouraged to use AI agents to find and patch issues, though deployment still takes weeks. The research firm Calif is mentioned as having used the Codex agent platform to find the Java4Shell vulnerability before the test. Other developers and infrastructure operators are affected as they are invited to help improve the open-source shields for the community. The tool helps defenders who cannot patch every single system immediately after a new vulnerability is discovered by AI models.

AI has been both a boon and a bane for security teams by surfacing more vulnerabilities and enabling new attacks. AI models have surfaced previously unknown vulnerabilities, which has given organizations a much shorter timeframe to send out necessary security patches. The articles state that testing and deploying patches typically takes days or weeks, leaving systems exposed to potential exploits in between. OpenAI and Cisco claim that AI-powered platforms like Shirudo are the first step toward building infrastructure that adapts to threats. This background explains the need for temporary safeguards that can be deployed quickly before a permanent software fix is available.

Next, the companies want to strengthen operating system foundations to deploy these protections at scale by hardening the kernel and services. They aim to limit workload permissions and make the processes for recovery and updates safer for all users of Linux. The open-source community will continue to build out patches while the companies provide tested shields alongside new vulnerability disclosures. The articles leave open how other operating systems besides Linux might eventually integrate this type of AI-powered shielding technology. It remains to be seen how widely the community will adopt the BSD 2-Clause licensed platform to protect global infrastructure.

stories.Summary:
Robert Izquierdo of The Motley Fool published a comparison of Advanced Micro Devices and Dell Technologies revenue trends on Nov. 23, 2026, at 12:02PM EST. The article appeared on fool.com at 06:00:00Z and was republished by AOL at 18:00:00Z the same day. It compared quarterly revenue for the two companies over the last eight quarters, using data from Financial Modeling Prep as of Nov. 20, 2026. AMD closed the World Labs acquisition on Nov. 16 and announced a partnership with Meta Platforms on Oct. 27. Dell partnered with Rackspace on Nov. 17 and collaborated with Mistral AI on Oct. 21.

AMD reported $7.7 billion in Q4 2024, for the quarter ended Dec. 28, 2024, and $7.4 billion in Q1 2025, ended March 29, 2025. It reported $7.7 billion in Q2 2025, ended June 28, 2025, $9.2 billion in Q3 2025, ended Sept. 27, 2025, and $10.3 billion in Q4 2025, ended Dec. 27, 2025. AMD reported $10.3 billion in Q1 2026, ended March 28, 2026, $11.5 billion in Q2 2026, ended June 27, 2026, and $13.4 billion in Q3 2026, ended Sept. 26, 2026. Dell reported $23.9 billion in Q4 2024, ended Jan. 31, 2025, $23.4 billion in Q1 2025, ended May 2, 2025, and $29.8 billion in Q2 2025, ended Aug. 1, 2025. Dell reported $27.0 billion in Q3 2025, ended Oct. 31, 2025, $33.4 billion in Q4 2025, ended Jan. 30, 2026, $43.8 billion in Q1 2026, ended May 1, 2026, and $47.0 billion in Q2 2026, ended July 31, 2026, while Q3 2026 was not yet reported.

AMD's management projected further acceleration in Q4, and AMD's year-over-year quarterly revenue growth rate stepped up from the low-to-mid 30% range throughout 2025 to an average of 44% across the first three quarters of 2026. Dell raised its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $192 billion, implying approximately 69% annual growth over fiscal 2026, thanks to a record $95 billion server backlog. AMD climbed 74.7% from $7.7 billion in Q4 2024 to $13.4 billion in Q3 2026, with management guiding for roughly $17 billion in Q4 2026. Dell generates more than triple AMD's trailing twelve-month revenue, about $151.2 billion versus $45.4 billion. Dell converts its AI server backlog into revenue at roughly 21% gross margins, while AMD captures 54% gross margins.

The article said Dell had significantly higher revenue than AMD in the last two years, that both experienced year-over-year sales increases, and that both are seeing revenue growth accelerate in 2026. It attributed Dell's higher absolute total to selling complete, high-ticket systems such as servers, data center hardware, and PCs, whereas AMD sells individual semiconductor components that go into those systems. It described the difference between a systems integrator such as Dell and AMD's fabless chip design approach. It said Dell's exposure to component cost inflation contrasts with AMD's upstream silicon pricing power. It said tracking revenue helps investors measure a company's ability to generate baseline sales before accounting for expenses.

The article said both companies quickly pivoted away from relying on cyclical PC markets to being anchored by enterprise and hyperscale AI infrastructure expansion as the artificial intelligence boom accelerated in 2026. It said Dell's top-line growth inflection came as its massive AI server backlog converted into shipments. It said AMD demonstrated a steady, compounding staircase in revenue. It said each incremental dollar of AMD data center revenue flows through to operating income at a much higher rate. It said the revenue trends reveal both companies are enjoying massive revenue boosts.

The article did not report Dell's Q3 2026 revenue, listing it as not yet reported. It left open whether AMD's management projection of further acceleration in Q4 would be met. It left open whether Dell's raised fiscal 2027 guidance of $192 billion would be achieved. It did not state when Dell's Q3 2026 results would be published. It did not give AMD's Q4 2026 quarter end date.

stories.Headline: OpenAI launches OpenWorks to give US small businesses free AI training
stories.Summary:
OpenAI launched OpenWorks on Monday, November 23, 2026, a nationwide initiative that connects small business owners with local AI experts for free, personalized, hands-on training, according to Live 5 News. The program was announced by OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company, and described by OpenWorks founder Jake Ottiger as a way to pair small business owners with local AI experts. Charleston, South Carolina, is among the communities where OpenAI is introducing the initiative, with help from Jim Reilly, who co-founded Charleston AI to teach individuals and businesses how to use artificial intelligence. OpenAI president and cofounder Greg Brockman described OpenWorks in a tweet as a program designed to fund local AI experts to help small businesses grow with AI. ZDNET reported that OpenAI launched OpenWorks on November 24, 2026, describing it as a nationwide network of OpenWorks Partners to provide free, hands-on AI support to small businesses.

Eligible independently owned small businesses in the US can apply and, if accepted, receive one-on-one support from a partner expert, help with tools they already use, and three free months of ChatGPT Business. OpenAI states that software and SaaS companies, venture-backed businesses, and private equity-owned businesses are not eligible. The pilot program is available in 20 communities, and according to a tweet by OpenAI's Jake Ottiger, OpenWorks is open only to communities in the US "for now." OpenAI pays partners up to $8,000 per month to provide local support and workshops, though the company does not specify how that number is arrived at or how much individual partners will be paid. Partners are asked to commit four full days per month to providing free, hands-on AI help to local small businesses, plus one monthly workshop.

Ottiger said the program is meant to pair small business owners with local AI experts to provide free hands-on help for AI, and that the primary goal is for small business owners to have the skills necessary to grow their businesses on their own terms going forward. Brockman said AI is accelerating small business, lowering the barriers to entry, and helping them earn more, noting he has been increasingly hearing from people who left their jobs to start a small business because they have AI tools to support them. Reilly said the first and foremost challenge is what he calls FUD, fear, uncertainty and doubt, and that once businesses move past those concerns, AI can help with customer outreach, marketing, reviewing documents, organizing information, and managing routine office work. Reilly said that in his own produce delivery business, what used to take three hours to do can be done in about 10 minutes, freeing up time for other things. OpenAI says it is looking for technically skilled and curious individuals and small teams committed to helping local businesses thrive, and that software and AI consultancies are encouraged to apply alongside their existing client work.

Ottiger said Ghost Grow 843, a microgreens company owned by Garrett Fleming, saw its sales conversion rate increase from 20% to 75% after adopting more targeted outreach methods, and that Fleming was knocking on fewer doors but the right doors. Reilly said Fleming was initially reluctant to use AI and had spent significant time visiting restaurants and speaking with chefs, and that ChatGPT helped identify restaurants across Charleston, James Island and Johns Island that might already be using microgreens, with work that could have taken hours completed in roughly 10 minutes. Ottiger recalled working with a woman who handled operations and sales for a sign manufacturing company and was overwhelmed with customer follow-ups, invoices and other responsibilities while caring for her child, and said the company generated approximately $10,000 in orders the following day. OpenAI spotlighted four businesses in its announcement: Tiny Things, a small gift shop that built a custom inventory dashboard connecting existing tools to keep popular products in stock; Ghost Grow 843, which gained new restaurant customers; Sign Badgers, a custom sign business that automated inventory tracking and vendor price checks and claims OpenWorks saved it 2 to 5 hours each week; and Black Paper Party, a gift wrap supplier that matched purchase orders with shipping records, discovered billing errors, and avoided thousands of dollars in potential chargebacks.

The reported increase reflects results shared by OpenWorks leadership. ZDNET reported that IBM set up a small business division in 1990 offering training and incentives for businesses adopting PC technology, and even set up pop-up stores inside the old Sears retail chain. In 1996, Microsoft created a small business technology partnership board and set up a $5 million fund in cash and software to help connect hundreds of small-business organizations across the country to the Internet. In 2017, Google set up a free workshop program for small businesses to help them learn how to use Google's tools for digital marketing.

ZDNET reported that the partner application asks, "Can you work in person?" and "Tell us where you can help in person," and that the program appears to be in-person focused. ZDNET noted that it remains unknown whether a virtual assistance program is planned for small businesses located outside urban centers. ZDNET reported that substantial gaps remain across the Mountain West and rural America on the program's availability map.

OpenAI asks partner applicants to be technically capable, collaborative, and motivated to give back to their community, and to propose ideas for what they would work on for their first community day and together with small businesses. OpenAI also asks applicants to list one or two client testimonials to show they can collaboratively work with small businesses. ZDNET reported that it is still unknown whether a virtual assistance program is planned for small businesses outside urban centers. ZDNET disclosed that Ziff Davis, its parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

stories.Headline: Enverus report finds AI uses less water per dollar than almond milk or golf
stories.Summary:
Enverus Intelligence Research published a report finding that artificial intelligence consumes less water per dollar spent than almond milk or golf, according to The Straits Times on Nov 25, 2026. The report, titled Data Center Water Use | Setting the Record Straight, compares water consumption using a consistent monthly spending benchmark across different activities. It puts US$25 (S$32) a month of AI spending at about 1.9 gallons of water consumption, including water used to generate the electricity that powers data centres. The same US$25 spent on almond milk consumes 308 gallons of water, while the same amount spent on golf course green fees consumes 679 gallons, the report says.

Household electricity on an all-natural-gas grid consumes about 31 gallons for the same spending, according to the report. About 90% of the water attributed to running AI models is consumed at power plants rather than data centres, the report found. Enverus said a modern hyperscale data centre campus consumes about 32,100 gallons of water per acre a month, less than rice, almonds or alfalfa, and similar to an average US golf course. The report compares water consumption using a consistent monthly spending benchmark.

Ryan Luther, director of Energy Transition Research at Enverus, said that if a typical consumer is worried about their water footprint, skipping one almond latte a week does more than giving up AI chatbots entirely. The report was published by Enverus Intelligence Research and reported by The Straits Times on Nov 25, 2026. The study compares water consumption across AI spending, almond milk, golf course green fees and household electricity on an all-natural-gas grid. The Straits Times reported the findings under the headline that AI consumes less water per dollar spent than almond milk or golf.

stories.Headline: Pinterest lets parents limit AI-generated content teens see
stories.Summary:
Pinterest announced this week that it is adding new parental controls for AI-generated content. The company introduced these updates on November 24, 2026, to help parents manage teen accounts. These changes allow parents to adjust the amount of AI-generated content in recommendations. The platform is expanding its existing tools to give parents more control over the experience. This update focuses specifically on the content that teenagers see while using the app.

Parents can now use an updated Parental Controls page to manage various settings for their children. They can tweak if videos autoplay and adjust the volume of push, browser, in-app, and email notifications. The redesigned page also allows parents to configure settings related to personalized ads for their teens. These tools are available on the Pinterest platform to help parents dictate the user experience. The update includes these standard options alongside the new AI-generated content limit settings.

Pinterest is responsible for these changes and claims to be one of the first major platforms to do this. The company says these tools allow users to dictate the type of experience they want on the app. They are providing these settings as part of an overall expansion of their parental control features. The company is putting these specific tools into the hands of parents to manage AI exposure. This move follows the company's own efforts to fight AI content within its user feeds.

Parents have said that the lack of AI controls is harming children's well-being in favor of profits. The children's advocacy group Fairplay expressed similar concerns in a letter sent in April to other tech leaders. Over 200 organizations and experts signed that letter to demand the removal of AI content for minors. Teens are the primary group affected by these new settings and the general presence of AI content. Other platforms like Snap and Meta have also implemented different limits for their younger users.

Pinterest introduced settings to restrict AI-modified content in 2025, but some AI content still appeared in feeds. Other platforms have focused on limiting access to AI chatbots or pausing access to AI characters. WhatsApp allows parents to adjust how teens use Meta AI to create content or ask questions. Most social media platforms generally provide few controls for AI-generated content filling user feeds and recommendations. These new Pinterest tools build upon the company's previous attempts to manage AI-generated material.

The new parental controls are now available for parents to use on the updated settings page. Parents can now limit the AI-generated content that appears in the recommendations for their teen children. The articles do not state when further updates to these parental controls will be released. It remains open whether these tools will fully stop AI content from appearing in teen feeds. The text does not mention if other social platforms will follow this specific model of control.

stories.Headline: Google launches Momentum to give Indian startups AI and cloud support
stories.Summary:
Google launched an initiative called Momentum on 24 November 2026 to deepen its support for Indian startups by giving them access to AI technologies, cloud infrastructure, engineering expertise and global platforms. The company said the initiative builds on a decade of its Google for Startups Accelerator programmes in India and is meant to help founders develop products, deploy AI solutions and expand into new markets. Google also said Momentum would bring together its technology, research and global networks to support Indian founders. The programme is designed to help startups move beyond product development into areas such as trusted AI deployment, customer acquisition, commercial readiness and expansion into new markets. In July, when it marked ten years of its accelerator programmes in India, Google said it had supported 277 Indian startups, with 94 per cent of its alumni continuing to build and scale their businesses.

As part of Momentum, Google cited several Indian startups using its technologies, including the healthcare startup AiSteth, which it said has screened more than 160,000 patients across over 20 Indian states using Gemini, MedGemma and Gemma for clinical summaries and medical training. Google said the legal tech company SpotDraft integrated Gemini with on-device capabilities through Chrome for its contract workflows, reducing latency by 70 per cent and processing costs by 80 per cent. Google also said VideoSDK built real-time conversational AI agents using the Gemini Live API and reported a 25 per cent improvement in response quality and a roughly 40 per cent reduction in infrastructure costs after moving to Google Cloud. Google highlighted startups developing AI models for Indian languages, including Shunya Labs, which supports more than 200 languages and dialects and has used Gemma models and Project Vaani speech data to develop specialised models such as an offline Hindi speech recognition model. Bengaluru-based ZenteiQ, a spinout from IISc, is developing small AI models for edge devices and increased its inference throughput fourfold using Google Cloud TPUs and Google Kubernetes Engine, according to Google.

Google said ZenteiQ has also been selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop foundation models covering English and 10 Indian languages. Google also cited Phot.ai, an AI-powered creative platform that uses Google Cloud to scale its infrastructure and Google Ads to improve customer acquisition. Google said its support extends beyond technology to infrastructure costs, customer acquisition, security and market expansion, and that security, privacy and responsible AI development will remain central to its work with Indian startups as they move towards wider adoption and deployment. The company also said it supports startups addressing scientific and environmental challenges through the AI for the Planet Accelerator, an initiative by Google DeepMind that provides access to frontier AI technology and technical expertise for climate, agriculture and environmental resilience applications. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the launch of the initiative and the support Google has described.

stories.Headline: Onclusive finds AI citations vary by category as Webflow reports median brands appear in 16% of AI answers
stories.Summary:
On November 25, 2026, The Drum published a member article by Aya Elbaoudi of Onclusive, a field marketing assistant, arguing that brands’ AI visibility problems are local, sectoral and specific. Onclusive analyzed 1,972 unique earned-source domains cited by five AI systems, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity and Grok. The analysis covered 12 industries, 24 categories and six countries: France, Italy, Mexico, Spain, the UK and the US. On November 24, 2026, IT Brief Australia published a report by news editor Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin on Webflow research finding most companies have limited visibility in AI answer engines. Webflow’s study found the median company appeared in 16% of responses across a sample of 2,000 websites.

Onclusive said the closer you get to the question your audience actually asks, the less the global list matters. Its analysis split the 12 industries into 24 product and service categories, and it said sources AI systems cite can change from one category to the next within the same industry. It said the top of its Industry Citation Guide is led by Il Sole 24 Ore, El Economista (Mexico) and Les Echos, ahead of Forbes and CNBC. It said Reddit appears in retail’s top sources nearly three times as often as in automotive’s, with about 29 mentions against 11. It said Toyota holds a 24.7% share of voice in hybrid SUVs and appears in 92.5% of AI answers there, while in electric cars its visibility drops to 1% and Tesla is chosen in 95% of answers.

Onclusive said B2B sectors such as banking, enterprise software, insurance and pharma lean on journalism, institutional sources and regulators. It said B2C sectors such as consumer tech, retail, fashion and travel draw more on reviews, creators and community discussion. It said regulated industries such as healthcare and telecoms are shaped heavily by government and policy sources. It said a source that dominates in the US might barely register in France, Italy or Spain. It said the same source can be essential context in one category and background noise in another.

Webflow said the median company was cited with a link only 6% of the time, and appeared 15% of the time whenever any company was mentioned. It said the systems got facts wrong roughly one-third of the time when a company was mentioned, producing an accuracy score of 63 out of 100, with message pull-through at 24 out of 100 and median sentiment at 57 out of 100. It said B2B SaaS and software companies were mentioned 20% of the time against 14% for B2B industrial and manufacturing groups, with citation rates of 13% and 6% respectively. It said companies in the Forbes AI 50 were mentioned 31% of the time against 16% across all 2,000 websites, and cited 8% of the time against 6%. It said Progressive had the strongest visibility in the Ad Age Top 50 US Ad Spenders group, with a mention rate of 44%.

Onclusive said its analysis identified 70 media sources linked to 220 articles where Toyota is either absent or described negatively, including Edmunds, KBB and Auto Express. It said its AI Visibility Playbook sets out six steps, from mapping cited sources to measuring change in AI answers over time, and includes a 90-day plan for PR, comms, content and digital teams. Webflow said its assessment covered 2,000 websites and used 123 scoring gates, drawing on roughly 325,000 lines of code, more than 29,000 automated tests, more than 5,200 lines of prompts and 100 source modules across more than 500 large language model sessions. Webflow said it queried four answer engines with buyer-style questions and scored responses against a common rubric, measuring quality metrics across the 1,579 domains mentioned at least once. Webflow said Forbes AI 50 companies’ content had been updated within the previous six months at three times the rate seen across the wider sample, and those businesses were recognised as thought leaders 60% more often.

Webflow ranked Krea.ai highest overall among the Forbes AI 50, followed by Abridge, BaseTen and Cohere, and ranked AllState highest in the Ad Age group, followed by Capital One, Pfizer and Progressive. It said none of the Cannes Grand Prix winners reviewed reached the top tier of its scoring, with Columbia, Heineken, Suncorp Insurance and Adidas ranking highest in that group. It said Google, represented by deepmind.google, ranked as the most mature in the MANGOS group of Meta, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google, OpenAI and SpaceX, with Nvidia following on a mention rate of 86%. Onclusive said the next phase of generative engine optimization is about finding the handful of sources that repeatedly shape the answers you want to influence in your industry, market and category. Webflow said that for many brands the issue is not only whether they appear in an answer, but whether the answer links back to them and describes them accurately.

stories.Headline: KPMG runs AI agents alongside humans in a FTSE 250 audit pilot
stories.Summary:
The Financial Reporting Council published guidance on 16 November 2026 on when insights produced by AI can threaten an auditor’s independence. Two days later the Financial Times reported that KPMG had run more than 100 AI agents through a FTSE 250 audit alongside its normal audit team. On 23 November 2026 Wendy Russell, who heads audit at Grant Thornton UK, told the FT that firms building the quickest, most automated audit at the cheapest price would harm the profession. The KPMG pilot was codenamed Project Exponential and put agents across every phase of the audit. A conventional audit by KPMG’s accountants ran alongside, and that was the one the firm relied on.

The FRC’s March 2026 guidance on generative and agentic AI says the human in an agentic system may set its goal, provide information, and oversee or review actions or outputs at specific control points. The same guidance warns that an auditor who exhibits automation bias at those control points can leave the system’s outputs deficient. The FRC’s 16 November guidance says technology-derived insights can pose distinct threats to the auditor’s integrity, objectivity or independence, especially where the work behind an insight falls outside the audit of the accounts. The FT reported that 83% of Grant Thornton staff use generative AI tools every week. The FT reported that Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC have together put billions behind the bet that AI will transform audit.

KPMG’s head of audit in the UK, Cath Burnet, called human involvement critical and said the system gives full visibility and full traceability of the agents’ work. Burnet said the technology cannot yet run thousands of audits, that some companies may prefer not to use the service, and that few have data clean enough for the agents. David Gartside, Grant Thornton’s chief digital officer, compared the risk to the automation complacency seen with partly driverless cars. Gartside said you cannot do 99 per cent of the work with an agent and then have a human drop in the last 1 per cent. Gartside said human goes first is the safest option.

Mark Babington, the FRC’s executive director of regulatory standards, said that whatever technology a firm uses, the auditor remains accountable. Babington said auditors need to be able to explain how they used it, challenge its outputs and stand behind the evidence. Russell said an audit is built from hundreds or thousands of minute judgments. Russell said you can have a race to the bottom or you can actually make the audit more high quality. Russell said that if you are using a tool that made a bad decision, you would have to question that decision and every other decision that tool made.

The FT describes an AI arms race between UK accounting firms that has pushed the largest further ahead of the mid-tier. The FT notes that audit firms have long charged clients for big teams of junior staff doing painstaking groundwork, with a few senior people supervising. KPMG acknowledged clear time-saving opportunities from its AI audit but would not say whether fees would come down. KPMG International, according to the same report, has secured lower fees from its own auditor on the grounds that AI will cut the cost of the work. The FT describes Grant Thornton’s alternative method as an experiment.

Grant Thornton says it has taken its concerns to the FRC, which set up a sandbox this year so firms can work through AI use. KPMG briefed the regulator on its experiment in outline. The FRC’s written guidance names neither firm’s method. The FRC’s March guidance calls the level of confidence an AI output needs a matter of professional judgement, use case by use case. The FT describes cognitive forcing as something Grant Thornton is experimenting with.

stories.Headline: Amata B.Grimm Power and NTT Global Data Centers study a 400MW AI data center campus in Thailand
stories.Summary:
B.Grimm announced on November 24, 2026 that B.Grimm Power had signed a memorandum of understanding with NTT Global Data Center to pursue a 400 MW data center opportunity in Thailand. The memorandum covers digital infrastructure, an AI ecosystem and energy infrastructure, with an investment value of approximately THB 113 billion. The memorandum is an agreement to pursue the opportunity, not a confirmation that construction has started. Nopadej Karnasuta, B.Grimm Power’s president for Thailand, Malaysia and Energy & Industrial Solutions Business, joined the Japan visit during which it was signed. B.Grimm dates the visit, led by Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas, to November 17, 21, 2026.

Amata B.Grimm Power, a subsidiary of B.Grimm Power (SET: BGRIM), signed the memorandum with NTT Global Data Centers (Thailand), part of NTT DATA, to jointly carry out a feasibility study for a 400MW hyperscale data center campus at Amata City Chonburi Industrial Estate. Investment in the project is estimated to exceed THB 113 billion, and it is expected to create more than 2,500 jobs. The memorandum was signed on Nov. 19 in Tokyo at the Thailand-Japan Investment and Business Dialogue 2026, organized by the Thailand Board of Investment and Japan's Keidanren business federation, with Ekniti presiding. A November 23, 2026 release from Thailand’s Board of Investment dates the Tokyo delegation to November 17, 20, 2026. The BOI, Keidanren dialogue drew 64 Japanese private-sector executives from 38 companies across nine industries.

Under the memorandum, Amata B.Grimm Power would develop the energy and utility infrastructure for the campus, while NTT GDC would bring its experience in data center design, construction and operation. The partners named cloud service providers, AI platform developers and global companies, including clients from Japan, the US and Europe, as target customers. Nopadej Karnasuta said the collaboration reflects a shared vision to develop stable and sustainable energy and digital infrastructure. B.Grimm Power’s company profile reports 5,180 MW of installed capacity and energy delivery through its own distribution networks to more than 400 industrial users. B.Grimm Power states a goal of secured power purchase agreements totaling 10,000 MW by 2030.

The delegation also visited NTT Data Mitaka EAST Data Center to study security, system continuity and energy efficiency in infrastructure supporting AI. B.Grimm’s account says Ekniti highlighted NTT’s Japanese facilities as efficient, quiet, environmentally considerate and able to coexist with local communities. Discussions at the dialogue covered three supply chains: modern vehicles; AI infrastructure and advanced electronics; and modern power grids. NTT DATA appointed Yasuhiro Kajiki on September 10, 2026, as managing director, Japan and APAC, for NTT Global Data Centers, responsible for regional operations and growth strategy. The company linked the expanded leadership role to growing customer demand for AI-ready digital infrastructure across APAC.

A separate agreement with Bloom Energy, announced on November 5, 2026, calls for NTT to deploy 900 MW of onsite power across multiple data center projects globally, with initial shipments planned for 2027. Doug Adams, CEO of NTT Global Data Centers, said clients are building AI capabilities at a pace the grid alone cannot always match, and that speed to power has become one of the defining factors in delivering capacity when and where it’s needed. In January, Amata B.Grimm Power signed a 100MW power purchase agreement with NTT Global Data Centers to supply NTT's fourth data center at Amata City Chonburi, scheduled to start commercial operation in June 2027. Amata B.Grimm Power also supplies electricity to NTT's second and third data centers in Thailand. On June 18, 2026, subsidiary B.Grimm BeyondBridge and INET established B.Grimm INET to develop and operate platforms in Thailand covering energy management, environmental and smart utility systems, greenhouse-gas monitoring and management, cloud security and AI technologies.

No final investment decision, construction start or completion date has been announced. The open question the articles raise is execution: whether the partners can combine NTT’s data center expansion with B.Grimm’s power operations and digital-infrastructure experience. B.Grimm Power also aims to uphold the practices highlighted during the Japan visit while sharing knowledge and technology with Thai people over the long term. NTT DATA expects Bloom’s modular fuel-cell systems to bring power online alongside construction and expand with increasingly power-dense AI workloads. The articles state that turning the investment-mission memorandum into operating AI infrastructure would require delivering the efficiency, quiet operation and community coexistence highlighted during the Japan visit.

stories.Headline: Galveston police adopt Veritone Investigate AI to speed active and cold case work
stories.Summary:
The Galveston Police Department announced in a November 19 news release that it will begin using an artificial intelligence platform called Veritone Investigate to help move active and long-running cold case investigations along more efficiently, according to Houston Public Media. The Galveston City Council approved the use of the AI-powered tools in a 5-0 vote at a council meeting on November 12. The service package with Veritone runs for one year and costs approximately $75,000, according to city documents. The California-based company Veritone works with about 450 agencies across the U.S. for public safety, most of which are in California, and CEO and President Ryan Steelberg said the partnership with Galveston is one of the company's first entry points into Texas.

Steelberg said police departments are struggling to manage increasing volumes of digital evidence, which makes it harder to find information that moves cases forward. He said the investigative tool would help agencies process audio, video, images and documents and make the material searchable, and would also use AI-driven tools to get information relevant to an investigation. He said the AI is not trying to solve the case for the department but is trying to organize the data. Galveston Police Chief Doug Balli said that entering just one case into Veritone would save the average investigator hundreds of man-hours in reviewing information and generating leads, and that investigators need technology that helps them move from evidence to insight quickly, especially when they are working both active and cold cases. Balli did not respond to Houston Public Media's request for comment about the new technology.

Steelberg said the information used with Veritone Investigate will be safeguarded like any other investigation and that the process for public records requests will not change. He said nothing will change in terms of the controls, audit logging and jurisdiction, and that the purpose is for data to go into a secure environment where the AI models that are invoked are containerized and secure. The department's decision comes alongside heavy scrutiny from residents around Harris and Galveston counties who have expressed privacy concerns about Flock Safety cameras, which use AI technology to automatically read license plates, especially in light of Houston-area cases of alleged misuse by law enforcement. It also comes around the same time that Harris County officials decided to pull a no-bid contract for a controversial AI facial recognition technology, Clearview AI, from a commissioners court meeting agenda.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following national security review
stories.Summary:
The board of NVIDIA unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director on November 23, 2026. This decision came eleven days after Huang resigned from his position on November 12, 2026. He had stepped down four days after admitting to an affair with a woman. Reports linked him to a former Megaspeed CEO alleged to work for Chinese intelligence.

The board reinstated Huang after meetings with him and receiving input from unnamed senior United States government officials. Colette Kress returns to her role as CFO after serving as the interim CEO. Harvey Jones remains the chair of the board during this leadership transition. The board also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors. They are currently hiring a chief compliance officer to manage company operations.

The board stated it was satisfied with the candor and ability of Huang to lead the company. They claimed his return poses no national security risk based on the government input received. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he convinced the board to bring Huang back. He stated that he urged the board directly and indirectly to make this decision.

The reversal of the resignation drew criticism from members of both parties in the United States Congress. Retired Brigadier General Robert Spalding said the severity of the national security risks is a matter of debate. He argued that the Chinese Communist Party is a grave threat to the West. He believes the United States must recognize how China uses technology to strengthen its industries.

Huang resigned amid reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. This occurred as senators and House leaders pressed for chip export records and a closed door briefing. About 600,000 NVIDIA H200s are reportedly held in Hong Kong awaiting import approval from Beijing. Samsung and SK hynix HBM is reportedly reaching Chinese AI chipmakers through smuggling. Oracle canceled an estimated seven billion dollar AI compute deal with Tencent.

Huang is due to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, 2026. He must also sit for interviews with three different House committees regarding chip diversion. An independent board investigation into the foreign intelligence effort will proceed until it reaches a conclusion. The articles leave open whether Huang's return will expose sensitive technology or complicate export restrictions. They do not state the final outcome of the ongoing independent board investigation.

stories.Headline: EU plans 50 billion euro fund to support AI and quantum computing firms
stories.Summary:
The European Union reportedly plans to create a massive technology fund on November 25, 2026. This initiative aims to provide significant financial backing for companies specializing in artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The organization intends to use this capital to support high-risk ventures within the European tech sector. These strategic investments are designed to foster innovation and growth across the continent.

The proposed Sovereign Tech Equity Fund requires the mobilization of up to 50 billion euros. This substantial amount of money will be used to make long-term bets on emerging technologies. The primary goal of the fund is to close the existing technological gap between Europe, the United States, and China. By targeting AI and quantum firms, the union hopes to strengthen its global competitiveness.

Sources cited by the Financial Times are responsible for revealing these internal plans to the public. These sources indicate that the fund is necessary to support high-risk bets that private investors might avoid. They suggest that the European Union must take a more aggressive approach to funding deep tech. The reports emphasize that this move is a strategic necessity for the region.

The broader context of this plan involves a global race for dominance in critical future technologies. The European Union believes that without such a fund, it will fall further behind its major global rivals. Future developments will likely depend on the formal approval and funding of this equity vehicle. The success of the initiative will be measured by the growth of European quantum and AI firms.

stories.Headline: LG CNS students develop AI safe travel service and assistive tools
stories.Summary:
High school students developed artificial intelligence services through an education program run by LG CNS. These students created tools to recommend safer routes home and support people with disabilities. LG CNS held the AI Genius Academy Challenge Day on November 20. The event took place at the LG Science Park headquarters in Magok, Seoul. LG CNS announced these results on November 23.

The program attracted 1,300 high school students, which is the largest number since 2021. Ten teams from 161 demonstrated projects, including a housing safety service for real estate contracts. Mirim Meister High School won the grand prize for a safe travel service called Gwiga ON. Sudo Electric Technical High School earned the top excellence award, and Gwangju Speer Girls' High School won an excellence award. The service analyzes safety information to recommend walking routes and notifies guardians upon arrival.

LG CNS operates the AI Genius Academy as a career-oriented education program for high school students. The company stated that it is expanding the curriculum to match advances in AI technology. Participants spend about one year studying coding, data analytics, and AI while completing team projects. This year, the company offered five subjects including generative AI, physical computing, and introductory Python. The curriculum also included an introductory AI course and a data analytics course.

The service aims to improve safety for pedestrians and students returning home late at night. Other projects included a humanoid robot for the cognitive and physical rehabilitation of older adults. Students also developed an AI-powered cane to guide visually impaired users during fires using vibrations. A panel of LG CNS experts and external specialists in AI and social contribution selected the winners. These judges evaluated the completed projects, the presentations, and the demonstrations.

The AI Genius Academy has been running since 2021 to provide AI education to students. The program focuses on practical application through team-based projects and technical study. This year's addition of a data analytics course expanded the total number of subjects to five. The program integrates various technologies to solve social problems for the elderly and disabled. It provides a structured path for students to learn data analytics and coding.

LG CNS plans to add a physical AI course to the curriculum next year. This new course will cover technology that allows AI to perform tasks through physical devices. It will specifically focus on the use of robots to execute real-world tasks. The articles do not state when the winning AI services will be released. They also leave open whether the other showcased projects will be further developed.

stories.Headline: Micron expands high-bandwidth memory production in Taiwan and Singapore
stories.Summary:
The United States chipmaker Micron is accelerating the expansion of its high-bandwidth memory production facilities in Taiwan and Singapore. The company brought the first piece of production equipment into its Singapore packaging plant on November 19, 2026. This move is part of a strategy to compete with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix in the sixth-generation memory market. Micron expects to begin initial production at the Singapore site in early 2027.

The expansion requires an estimated investment of 7 billion dollars for the packaging facility alone. Micron reported capital spending of about 25 billion dollars for the first half of fiscal year 2027, which runs from September 2026 to August 2027. The company plans to increase this spending further in the second half of that period, primarily for cleanroom construction starting from the end of 2028. The Singapore packaging plant is expected to create around 1,400 jobs, while a separate wafer fabrication facility will add more for a total of 3,000 new positions.

Chen Kok Sing, a senior vice president at Micron, stated that the facility will strengthen the global assembly and test network. He noted that the progress reflects strong execution by company teams and close collaboration with partners like the Singapore Economic Development Board. Micron also claimed it began mass production of 12-layer HBM4 in March, with speeds exceeding 11 gigabits per second per pin. The company is currently providing customers with samples of a 16-layer product.

This expansion follows the claim by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that three memory chipmakers passed HBM4 certification for Vera Rubin. Micron is currently third in market share, with Counterpoint Research estimating its share at 18 percent in the second quarter of 2024. The company expects the Singapore production line to contribute meaningfully to its packaging capacity starting in the first half of 2027. Industry observers suggest these moves indicate that Micron has reached supply agreements with major buyers like Google and Nvidia.

stories.Headline: Cloudera launches a digital sovereignty package with Mistral AI models for governed data and AI
stories.Summary:
Cloudera Inc. announced a digital sovereignty package on November 24, 2026, which it said enables organizations to keep control of their data, artificial intelligence models and computing infrastructure wherever workloads run. The announcement was dated 06:00 UTC by SiliconANGLE and carried by GlobeNewswire from San Jose, California, and Madrid. Cloudera said the offering combines its Anywhere Cloud, Open Data Lakehouse and Unified Data Fabric technologies with open-weight AI models and model customization tools from Mistral AI SAS. Cloudera recently partnered with Mistral, and the integrated offering supports deployment across sovereign clouds, private data centers and fully air-gapped environments with no connection to external networks. Cloudera described the package as a comprehensive solution and partner ecosystem designed to give organizations jurisdictional, operational and technical control across their data, cloud and AI lifecycle.

The solution provides consistent zero-trust access controls, data lineage tracking and governance policies across deployment environments, according to Cloudera. Cloudera said these capabilities are intended to help organizations address requirements imposed by the European Union's AI Act, the Digital Operational Resilience Act and the Network and Information Security Directive, among other regulations. The Manila Times report said the solution supports compliance readiness for the EU AI Act, DORA, CADA, NIS2, the Seals Sovereignty Framework and others globally. Cloudera said governance policies also extend to enterprise data that AI agents retrieve and use, and that Mistral's open-weight models can run alongside governed data so organizations can customize models locally and run agentic workflows without exposing sensitive information. Cloudera said its modular hybrid cloud architecture lets users shift computing workloads between infrastructure providers and private data centers without rewriting applications or migrating or duplicating underlying data, and that organizations can apply sovereignty controls selectively to sensitive workloads.

Cloudera Chief Technology Officer Sergio Gago said enterprises need to know their data, models and infrastructure can remain under their control even as technology and regulatory requirements change. Gago said digital sovereignty has to be an architectural decision rather than a compliance exercise after the fact. He said Cloudera is giving organizations a foundation they can build on for the long term so they can adopt the next generation of AI without rethinking their sovereignty strategy each time the technology evolves. Gago said AI is becoming more autonomous and embedded in critical operations. Cloudera said the solution is built on open standards and an open source foundation and allows organizations to determine where individual workloads run and adapt without forced data migrations or proprietary lock-in.

Moor Insights & Strategy Chief Analyst Patrick Moorhead said AI has raised the bar on data protection. Moorhead said a company can meet every line of its sovereignty policy and still not control who accesses its data or who can turn off the models it depends on. He said walling off sensitive workloads is not the answer because it makes data and AI harder to manage, and he called extending Cloudera's hybrid data management to open-weight models across sovereign, on-prem and public cloud a logical step. Moorhead said the next step is how quickly customers get the offering into production. Cloudera said regulation, privacy and data sovereignty requirements rank among the top three barriers to scaling AI, and the offering is aimed at organizations facing those requirements.

McKinsey & Co. reported last year that 71% of executives it surveyed called sovereign AI an existential concern or a strategic imperative, according to SiliconANGLE. Cloudera said its own research found regulation, privacy and data sovereignty requirements among the top three barriers to scaling AI. Cloudera said digital sovereignty is becoming more pressing as enterprises move beyond managing data residency to ensuring the AI models and infrastructure they depend on remain under their control. Cloudera said it will supplement its Mistral partnership with an ecosystem of sovereign cloud providers and implementation partners. Cloudera said it is initially targeting Europe.

Cloudera plans to expand its sovereign partner ecosystem into other regions and regulatory jurisdictions globally after its initial focus on Europe. Cloudera said customers can combine sovereign deployments with other cloud and on-premises infrastructure and apply strict sovereignty controls where required without forcing the rest of their data estate into the same architecture or creating isolated security boundaries. The articles did not say when the offering becomes generally available or how it is priced. The articles did not name the sovereign cloud providers or implementation partners in the network. The articles did not say which specific Mistral models are integrated.
